findings.reason: Untrusted source: packets traversing the Bluetooth 6LoWPAN/IPSP netdev reach bt_xmit()/send_pkt(); remote peers can induce locally generated IPv6 traffic (ICMPv6/NDP replies) on this interface. Violated invariant: send_pkt() stores the skb pointer into channel-lifetime state at line 438 ('chan->data = skb;', comment 'Remember the skb so that we can send EAGAIN to the caller') without transferring ownership; bt_xmit() then unconditionally calls dev_kfree_skb(skb) at line 538 after send_pkt() returns, so chan->data retains a pointer to the freed sk_buff for the life of the l2cap_chan; send_mcast_pkt() (lines 479-488) repeats this per peer via local_skb followed by kfree_skb(local_skb). Unsafe use: any later reader of chan->data for an IPSP channel would dereference freed slab memory. Counterevidence checked: grep over net/bluetooth shows no reader of chan->data in 6lowpan.c (only the writer at 438) and the readers in l2cap_sock.c/smp.c/a2mp.c belong to socket/SMP/AMP channels, so the dangling pointer is currently latent; reported as a hypothesis with low confidence, no exploit claim.
findings.conclusion: bt_xmit() frees the skb (dev_kfree_skb, net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:538) while send_pkt() saved that skb pointer into long-lived l2cap channel state (chan->data = skb, line 438), leaving a dangling stored pointer; no in-tree reader found, so the UAF is latent.

candidates.reason: hdr = virtio_vsock_hdr(skb) is saved at 204, but both kfree_skb(skb) sites (209 and 215) immediately 'goto out_rcu' with no later hdr dereference in the function; hdr->dst_cid at 214 is read while the skb is still alive.
candidates.conclusion: No post-free use: every kfree_skb branch exits before touching hdr again.

candidates.reason: rq_arg.head[0].iov_base = skb->data is paired with rqstp->rq_xprt_ctxt = skb (ownership deliberately transferred, skb freed only after the RPC reply), and the nonlinear path consume_skb(skb) happens after the data was copied out via csum_partial_copy_to_xdr.
candidates.conclusion: Ownership transfer is explicit and the skb outlives its last data use; not a UAF.

candidates.reason: ip_version = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, 1, &buf) is dereferenced (*ip_version >> 4) strictly before netif_rx(skb) hands the skb to the stack; after netif_rx only the previously saved integer pktlen is used.
candidates.conclusion: Header pointer used before handoff, only a scalar used after; safe.

candidates.reason: In ipv6_srh_rcv/ipv6_rpl_rcv/ipv6_rthdr_rcv every kfree_skb(skb) error path returns -1 immediately (netif_rx(skb) at 413/523 also returns -1), and after pskb_expand_head the header pointer is refetched via hdr = (struct ... *)skb_transport_header(skb) at 441, 505 and 759 before further use.
candidates.conclusion: All frees are on paths that return; header pointers are refetched after head expansion; safe for this branch.

candidates.reason: kfree_skb(skb); skb = skbn; skb->data[14]--; dereferences the fresh skb_copy_expand() copy, never the freed original skb.
candidates.conclusion: Use targets the replacement skb; safe.

candidates.reason: skb_queue_tail(&hdev->raw_q, skb) and the later get_unaligned_le16(skb->data) at 1874 are in mutually exclusive if/else-if branches.
candidates.conclusion: Branch structure prevents any post-handoff data read; safe.

candidates.reason: consume_skb(skb); return NF_STOLEN; exits the branch before the th->ack dereference at 52 which lives in the else-if path (same shape in net/ipv4/netfilter/ipt_SYNPROXY.c and nf_synproxy_core.c).
candidates.conclusion: Free and th dereference are on exclusive paths; safe.

candidates.reason: skb_queue_tail(&dev->pending, skb); return; - the tty_insert_flip_string(&dev->port, skb->data, skb->len) at 619 is in the mutually exclusive else path, and the queued skb itself stays alive.
candidates.conclusion: Queue path returns immediately; data use is on the other branch; safe.

candidates.reason: The skb_queue_tail(&adapter->tx_data_q, skb) path returns 0 immediately; the local_tx_pd->flags write at the out: label is only reached on the host_to_card error path where the skb was never queued or freed, and this is the TX path not packet reception.
candidates.conclusion: No free-before-use on any single path; TX path only; safe.

candidates.reason: ptr = skb->data is consumed by wl1271_cmd_template_set(), which memcpy's from it into a freshly kzalloc'd command buffer before the caller's dev_kfree_skb(skb) at 1080.
candidates.conclusion: Data is copied out before the free; safe.

candidates.reason: chan->data = skb stores the skb into l2cap channel state that outlives the xmit call, after which bt_xmit() (line 538) and send_mcast_pkt() (line 487) free that same skb; the dangling pointer is never read for IPSP channels in this tree, so this is the reported low-confidence latent finding.
candidates.conclusion: Stored skb pointer outlives its dev_kfree_skb; no reader found, latent dangling state.

coverage_gaps: drivers/net/ was only sampled (hits from the '= skb->data' and queue/handoff-then-use greps over USB, PPP, wwan and wireless drivers); the ~2900 kfree_skb sites there were not all individually audited.

Free/use pairs separated by more than the 6-12 line heuristic window, or where the free happens inside a helper (netif_rx backlog drop, icmpv6_send, dev_queue_xmit completion, driver TX completion), were not exhaustively traced.
skb pointers stored inside driver/firmware private structs (e.g. ps->tx_skb in drivers/net/dsa/mv88e6xxx/hwtstamp.c) were only spot-checked, not lifetime-traced to their freeing path.
pskb_may_pull/pskb_expand_head head-reallocation stale-pointer sites were deliberately excluded per branch instructions (other branches cover them).
limitations: The single finding is a stored dangling pointer with no demonstrated dereference site: chan->data is written at net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:438 but never read for IPSP channels in this snapshot, so no crash or disclosure is proven; it is reported as a hypothesis with low confidence.
No build, KASAN or reproducer run was performed (read-only source snapshot, work confined to grep/reading), so all conclusions rest on static reading of this snapshot's exact lines.
Snapshot revision is opaque (hidden); line numbers and code state are valid only for snapshots/s01 as supplied.
